articles.title: Designing agent-first platforms: What changes when agents do the work
articles.summary: For decades, applications have been designed to wait. A user clicks, a request arrives, code runs, a response goes back. And we got very good at this. We learned to forecast traffic, scale on demand, wrap everything in enterprise controls, and run it all with the operational discipline that keeps critical business systems available around the clock. That model is being turned on its head, and being asked to serve apps that continuously act, and wait for no one. articles.title: Contrary to some reports, you don't have two brains
articles.summary: Late last week, we started seeing headlines about how new research was suggesting we might have two brains instead of the one that seems to show up on MRI scans. As is so often the case, these rumors can be traced back to a single press release put out by one of the universities where the work was done. You do not have two brains. It's a silly way to look at the results of the new paper. But there are far better ways to look at the results, ways that can help us understand how the brain gets put together and illustrate some of the general ideas behind developmental biology. So let's take a look at what the research actually shows and place it in the context of brain development. Read full article Comments

articles.summary: Agentic AI plays an important role in chip and system design, but not every “ agentic ” capability has the same degree of autonomy. In practice, autonomy is not binary. articles.title: Data privacy isn’t just for nerds — here’s why you should care too
articles.summary: A lot of times when I’ve mentioned moving to more privacy-focused apps and services, the reaction is more than a shrug — it’s a declaration that online privacy isn’t all that important. Most recently, at a tech event, I mentioned moving to Brave to avoid Google’s data collection and targeted advertising, and another attendee said that it’s just not important to them. That’s when I realized that there’s this general misunderstanding that prioritizing data privacy is the pastime of nerds and those prone to donning tin foil hats. I know I was someone who used to take a more laissez-faire approach to my online privacy. Years later, after grappling with the consequences of this, I feel that data privacy and data collection should be something everyone cares about.

articles.title: Review: Apple's hyper-pricey M5 Ultra Mac Studio made me into a vibe coder
articles.summary: This spring, Apple made it official: The Mac Pro is dead . When Apple was using Intel processors and AMD GPUs, the idea of an expandable and upgradeable tower made sense. But Apple Silicon chips bring the CPU, GPU, and memory interface all under one roof in a way that makes that sort of upgradeability not just superfluous but impossible. At least not without breaking some of the chips' key benefits. And as it happens, Apple Silicon's combination of a fast CPU, solid GPU, and unified memory architecture has made it a good fit for a modern "pro" workload that really pushes high-end hardware: running language models and agents locally.
